_description: Task13 DRIFT field, COARSE transcription -- the 0.55mm far-field grid for the 5x5 LArPix v2a tile at the true 4.4mm pitch, 15cm drift. The fine sibling (example_gen_pcb_drift_pixel_task13_fine.json) carries the true design values unsnapped. PHASE 4 RETARGET: this file was the 0.22mm / 79.15mm-deep / 56.0 V/mm transcription. Two measurements moved it (scripts/NOTES-run-pixel-field-seam.md): 0.22mm was far too fine for the bulk, because the far field is essentially 1-D linear out there and linear fields are exact on ANY spacing, so the resolution bought nothing; and the near/far interface at 19.8mm was measured sitting INSIDE the corrugated zone for the weighting field (transverse corrugation 40% of the local W on the seam plane), which no number of Schwarz sweeps can fix. The interface moves out to 29.7mm and the coarse grid relaxes to 0.55mm. THE BULK FIELD IS NOW 50.0 V/mm, NOT 56.0 -- READ THIS BEFORE 'RESTORING' ANYTHING. CathodePotential = -BulkField * (driftZDepth - pixelPlaneLowEdgePosition) = -50.0 * (149.55 - 9.9) = -6982.5 V. This is a DELIBERATE change of the design field, not a rescaling that preserves it. The previous -3878 V existed specifically to hold 56.0 V/mm across the 8cm geometry (and before that -8400 V held it across 15cm at the old 159.9mm depth). That choice has been GIVEN UP here. Do not 'fix' this back to 56.0 V/mm: drift velocities and induced currents from this geometry are NOT comparable to the 8cm results, because velo derives mobility from E through a nonlinear LAr parameterisation, so a 10.7% lower field is not a 10.7% slower drift. The value is maintained BY HAND on purpose, so the bulk field stays a visible, editable number rather than a derived one. The SAME voltage is applied on the coarse and the fine grid, deliberately: it is a boundary condition. 1.1mm IS THE SHARED PERIOD of the 0.55mm and 0.1mm grids -- the two grids share nodes only every 1.1mm -- and every plane that must land on both is a whole multiple of it: pitch 4.4 = 4x1.1 (8 coarse / 44 fine cells), pad plane 9.9 = 9x1.1 (18 / 99), interface 29.7 = 27x1.1 (54 / 297), cathode 149.6 = 136x1.1 (272 / 1496). That rule is the constraint to respect if any of them is moved. SNAPPED PAD/GAP, AND WHY ONLY HERE: the design values are pixelSize 3.5, pixelGap 0.9, chamfer_r 0.7, preserved as the _design_* keys below (the generators ignore _design_* keys). gcd(35,9) = 1, so NO spacing coarser than 0.1mm divides both the pad and the gap exactly and some snapping on the coarse grid is unavoidable. CELL COUNTS AT 0.55mm: pixelSize 3.30 -> 6 cells, pixelGap 1.10 -> 2 cells, chamfer_r 0.55 -> 1 cell (0.7/0.55 = 1.27). PITCH MUST STAY EXACTLY 4.4mm = 8 coarse cells: 6 + 2 = 8. hybrid_iterate.py _cells() requires the transverse extent to be a WHOLE number of cells and raises otherwise, so this is a hard constraint, not a preference. THE PRICE OF COARSENING, STATED PLAINLY: the pad area is (3.30/4.4)^2 = 0.5625 against the fine grid's (3.5/4.4)^2 = 0.6327, i.e. -11.1%. That is MUCH worse than the 0.22mm grid's +1.1%, and it matters for the same reason: the far field in the final stitched output IS the upsampled coarse solution, so a coarse pad-area error biases the far field by roughly the same percentage, and it is a SMOOTH error that the Laplacian residual metric cannot detect. The chamfer is undercut 21% (0.55 against 0.7). padThickness and FR4Thickness are both 0.55 so each rounds to exactly ONE cell: the generator derives pp_width = n_pad + n_fr4 - 1 = 1, putting the coarse pad TOP at (18+1)*0.55 = 10.45mm against the fine grid's 10.00mm. The two grids therefore model measurably different pads -- more so than at 0.22mm. EXPECTATION, NOT A MEASUREMENT -- for Phase 4/Step 6 to fill in: the coarse/fine far-field E_z spread should be substantially LARGER than the 0.199% measured on the 8cm / 0.22mm geometry, because both the pad-area snap (-11.1% vs +1.1%) and the pad-top offset (0.45mm vs 0.12mm) got worse. NO far-field E_z has been measured on this geometry. Every 'measured' figure from the 8cm transcription (55.996 V/mm coarse, 55.885 fine, the 0.199% spread, the 56.138/56.040 chord numbers, the 46.374 V/mm with-grid figure, the 10.56mm coarse pad top) has been DELETED rather than carried over, because none of it transfers: different depth, different spacing, different field, different pad snap. Do not reinstate any of it, and do not write a new number here until it has actually been solved for. WHAT MUST AGREE BETWEEN THE FILES, precisely: it is the FINE pair -- this field's fine config and the weighting field's fine config -- that must agree about the pad surface, because both fields' NEAR solves and ALL drift paths live on the 0.1mm grid, where the pad top is 10.00mm in both. Each COARSE file only supplies the far field beyond the 29.7mm interface, where the pad's discretisation no longer shapes the geometry, only the far amplitude. (Both fields do happen to share the 0.55mm coarse spacing here, so the two coarse files also agree -- but that is a coincidence of this geometry, not the reason it matters.) DEPTH: driftZDepth 149.55 is the electron LAUNCH node and is deliberately NOT rounded to 149.6. The key is overloaded -- it sets both the grounded cathode node and the path start z in continuous mm. hybrid_iterate._extents puts the cathode at ceil((driftZDepth + MIN_CATHODE_CLEARANCE)/coarse) = ceil(149.55/0.55) = 272 coarse cells = 149.6mm, the last plane of the 273-node coarse z grid and of the 1497-node fine grid (1496 fine cells), so there is NO dead space above the cathode; but the launch node 149.55 does not land on that grounded Dirichlet plane, which is what we want. MIN_CATHODE_CLEARANCE is 0.0, so the ceil alone provides the clearance, and it does so only because 149.55/0.55 = 271.9... is not already a whole number. Snapping driftZDepth would put the drift start exactly on the cathode. PAD PLANE 9.9 IS EXACT ON BOTH GRIDS: 9.9/0.55 = 18.0 and 9.9/0.1 = 99.0 with no floating-point shortfall, so the bare int() at gen_pcb_drift_pixel_with_grid.py:474 is safe on either. pixelPlaneWidth 0.55 is INERT in this configuration and is kept only in step with the spacing for readability: with enableInsulatorFR4 true and both padThickness and FR4Thickness present, the generator DERIVES pp_width = n_pad + n_fr4 - 1 and overwrites whatever this key says. THE SHIELD GRID IS OFF (GridHoleShape 'None'): it was inherited from the older with-grid task13 work and was never intended here -- the LArPix v2a 5x5 tile is a WOGRID geometry in production (commits a3d5e2c, 413460d). GridPotential, PcbWidth and HoleRadius are inert and are left in place: with 'None' neither the circular nor the square branch runs, and gridPotential is a DEAD PARAMETER of draw_pixel_plane -- it appears in that function's signature and docstring but nowhere in its body. GridPotential does NOT enter the cathode calculation. TILE SIZE: Npixels 5, i.e. a 5x5 pad tile at the 4.4mm pitch = 22.0mm transverse for the weighting probe; the DRIFT field is one periodic tile, so Npixels does not size this file's domain. THE test/ COPIES NOW DIVERGE FURTHER. The four task13 configs under scripts/ are retargeted to this geometry; their same-named copies in test/ are NOT, and test/run-task13-hybrid.sh still solves an older geometry. The cmp recipe in run-pixel-field.sh's header will report all four pairs as differing; that is expected, not a mistake to 'fix' by copying either way.
